title: Dynamic reservation SLO buffer and approval orchestration
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers requesting Dedicated reservations frequently under- or over-provision based on peak forecasts. Current intake produces a single static reservation size and a manual approval flow that doesn't account for transient bursts, autoscaling headroom, or cross-reservation placement constraints. This leads to: (a) unexpected throttling for latency-sensitive routes during short spikes, (b) over-reserving expensive GPU capacity, and (c) long approval cycles that block onboardings.

Proposal: Introduce a dynamic reservation orchestration that combines: (1) an SLO-backed throughput buffer (configurable percent headroom) attached to each reservation, (2) tiered autoscaling policy templates (conservative / balanced / aggressive) surfaced in the intake form, and (3) an approval orchestration that auto-simulates capacity impact and surfaces a recommended approver chain and SLA delta. The system will emit a recommended reservation contract that includes a guaranteed baseline, ephemeral burst allowance (metered), and a decommitment window tied to utilization history.

Goals: Provide predictable latency for customers with throughput guarantees while minimizing committed spend and reducing approval latency.

Out of scope: billing UI changes, enforcement of legal terms for multi-year contracts (handled by sales/legal), and deep changes to the serving runtime kernel selection.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form supports selecting autoscaling template and SLO buffer percentage
Capacity simulator runs during intake and returns a recommended baseline and burst allowance with cost delta
Approval orchestration surfaces recommended approvers and an automated escalation after 48h
Console shows reservation breakdown: baseline committed RPS, burst allowance (metered), SLO buffer, and historical utilization projection
E2E controlled rollout with 3 pilot customers verifies latency SLOs preserved under simulated spikes
rollout_plan: Design: finalize intake schema and autoscaling templates (2 weeks)
Engineering: implement simulator + API endpoints and attach SLO buffer to reservation model (3 sprints)
Pilot: enable for 3 customers with varying workload profiles and collect 4 weeks of telemetry
Iterate: adjust default buffer percent and autoscaling thresholds based on pilot feedback
Rollout: staged enablement for new reservations, migrate willing existing reservations behind feature flag
risks_mitigation: Risk: Overly large SLO buffer increases committed spend — Mitigation: default buffer set conservatively (5%) and require explicit opt-in for >15%
Risk: Simulator inaccuracies under novel workloads — Mitigation: limit initial rollout to controlled pilot and require an explicit ‘safety multiplier’ in intake
Risk: Approval automation misroutes approvals — Mitigation: human override path and audit trail for every automated decision
Risk: Metering burst allowance billing complexity — Mitigation: coordinate with billing to represent burst as separate metered line item; flag for follow-up billing project
